claims.statement: create_app builds the FastAPI app with AuthMiddleware added before CORSMiddleware so CORS wraps auth (preflights answered first, 401s carry CORS headers); allowed_origin_regex is passed as None when blank because an empty pattern would match every origin; FastAPI's own OTel tracing is disabled; Postgres InsufficientPrivilege maps to a 403 'Not allowed'.

AuthMiddleware is plain ASGI (not BaseHTTPMiddleware, to avoid buffering streaming chat), skips /health, /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json, resolves the caller once per request and stores principal plus db_role/db_claims on request state; get_caller_pool builds a CallerPool from them (anon with empty claims if absent) so PoolDep queries run in a transaction with SET LOCAL role anon or authenticated and JWT claims, returning the connection to the pool as owner.

api/router.py is the single REST mount point: one APIRouter with prefix /api including all per-resource routers (including registry, proposals and partner_groups), with OPENAPI_TAGS fixing doc order; /health and the three AG-UI chat routes /agent, /ingest and /proposal sit outside /api.

core/config.py's Settings is the only place defaults are written; a before-validator converts blank or whitespace values into the field default for the model specs, max_parallel_research, research_page_limit, research_model_call_limit, ask_model_call_limit and db_pool_max_size, because docker-compose forwards unset vars as empty strings that would otherwise break int parsing and boot.

Model tiers: MODEL (claude-opus-5-5) drives Ask's main agent and the Import supervisor; RESEARCH_MODEL (claude-sonnet-5-5) drives the entity-researcher and vault-reader subagents, the news grouping model and news verifier; UTILITY_MODEL (claude-haiku-4-5) drives catalog-writer, workbook-reader, rubric/summarizer, run_import_now extraction, live_status and news classifiers; SQL_AUDIT_MODEL (haiku) powers Ask's answer audit, and 'off' disables it.

fallback(primary, *candidates) adds one ModelFallbackMiddleware using the first candidate spec that differs from the primary (none if all match); Import subagents and supervisor and Ask's agent use it so a failed call moves to the next tier, with the strong model as the last fallback for subagents, and the researcher only gets EscalateAfterFailedSave when its research spec differs from MODEL.

db_pool_max_size (default 10) bounds one shared psycopg pool used by REST, agent tools and the checkpointer, and db_gate_slots is max(2, pool-3) so concurrency gates sit under the pool and do not starve the checkpointer; recursion_limit defaults to 200 because each middleware hook is its own graph node.

Feature switches derive from Settings properties: auth_enabled needs supabase_url, storage_enabled needs url plus service key, graph_enabled needs neo4j_uri and an OpenAI key, langfuse_enabled needs both Langfuse keys.

core/egress.py guarded_client refuses every outbound request, including redirect hops, to non-http(s), localhost, single-label, unresolvable, loopback, private, link-local or internal hosts (including numeric host forms and IPv6 embeddings of private IPv4), and refuses when it cannot decide; its callers are Import's download_file tool, the robots.txt/access checks in ingest/access.py and the RFP call pull. Ask has no fetch_url tool any more.

The MCP settings (github_pat, github_mcp_url, playwright_mcp_url, mcp_servers, github_tool_allowlist) are read only by app/agent/tools/mcp.py, and nothing under backend/app imports that module or calls load_mcp_tools, so they currently have no effect on the running agents.

The lifespan boots only what REST needs, in order: open the shared pool and publish it, verify the SQL catalog, open Graphiti, open the Postgres checkpointer, set app state with agents=None and an agents_lock, register a route for each path in AGENT_NAMES (/agent, /ingest, /proposal), and log boot timings; shutdown flushes Langfuse only if agents were built, then clears the pool.
Boot raises RuntimeError and refuses to start when the SQL tool catalog drifts from the database; tables merely undeclared are only logged at info level.

Agents are built lazily: load_agents builds all three agents (Ask, Import, proposal) once under agents_lock on the first request that needs one, calling configure_langfuse before the builders so the mask is registered first, wrapping each graph in SessionScopedAGUIAgent (/ingest with emit_subagent_events=True) and passing recursion_limit as the AG-UI config; get_graph builds them on demand for REST routes (ingest, threads and proposals messages).

The /agent, /ingest and /proposal POST routes are custom, replacing add_langgraph_fastapi_endpoint which needs a built agent at registration; they clone the AG-UI agent per request because it keeps per-run state, and each exposes GET {path}/health for smoke tests.

REST modules must not import agent code at module top level so a REST cold start avoids deepagents, model clients and tracing; routes such as threads.py defer heavy imports inside functions, and the first chat turn pays the deferred build cost.

configure_langfuse builds the client once with mask and span filter, aborts reporting tracing as not live if the client's mask is not mask_payload (first construction wins per public key) or if auth_check fails (wrong keys otherwise fail silently with a 401 on a background thread), and never raises so telemetry cannot take the app down.

trace_config always sets run_name, and when Langfuse is enabled attaches a handler and metadata with trace name and tags (sangam, agent tags, settings.model); trace roots are sangam_ask for Ask, sangam_import for Import and sangam_news_verify for the news verifier, with sangam_agent only the default.

mask_payload clips every string to 4,000 chars and, when LANGFUSE_MASK_TOOL_RESULTS is true, redacts warehouse rows after a 'columns: ' header or 'as stored:' line while keeping the query, caveats and sources; a failing mask sends the payload unmasked; export_span drops FastAPI HTTP spans and empty middleware hook spans.

The Langfuse handler subclass types graph and subagent runs as agent and the answer_audit hook as evaluator, sets root input to the last question and root output to the final tool-free replies (noting pending approvals), re-parents orphaned runs onto LangGraph node runs, and ends cancelled turns without an error level.

SessionScopedAGUIAgent maps the AG-UI thread_id to langfuse_session_id, the chat user to langfuse_user_id and run id to agui_run_id, de-duplicates re-sent tool results, addresses legacy resumes to one open interrupt via key_resume for parallel Import pauses, and flushes Langfuse in a thread after every run because a serverless function freezes after responding.

sql_span and traced_fetch record each SQL statement as a retriever observation under the current tool span with dedented SQL, params and row count, and score_answer attaches scores to the current turn's trace; both degrade to no-ops when tracing is unavailable.

recursion_limit must be passed both bound to the graph and as the AG-UI agent's config, because AG-UI builds each request config with ensure_config which stamps LangGraph's default of 25 over the graph-bound value; tests pin the trap and require the setting to stay at least 150.
langsmith_status only reports at boot whether LangSmith tracing is enabled, off or missing a key; LangSmith itself is switched on by environment variables with no code wiring.

Deploy topology: both Vercel projects set git.deploymentEnabled false and region bom1; the backend function app/main.py has maxDuration 1800 and a cron hitting /health every 5 minutes to keep one instance warm.

Performance history: moving both functions to bom1 beside Supabase cut warm /api/funders from 1.2 s to 0.2 s; cold starts (8-12 s, with the agent stack about two-thirds of import time) drove lazy agent loading, aggregate profile and ingest overview endpoints, and a signed-out Next data cache with revalidate 300; the runtime dependency install remains because graphiti-core stays.

Known regression: #178 removed emit_raw_events=False from the Ask and Import agents in core/lifespan.py, so SessionScopedAGUIAgent (which defaults emit_raw_events=True) again streams raw LangGraph events on /agent and /ingest, after the flag had cut one answer from 1.69 MB to 107 KB; /proposal is still built with emit_raw_events=False; the changelog lists it under 'Not finished'.

Chat access is per route via AGENT_ACCESS keyed by path (a missing path fails at boot): /agent uses ask_access (sign-in, thread ownership with 404 for others' threads staff included, and sets agent_caller plus a fresh caveats_given set so Ask's SQL runs as the caller); /ingest uses require_scout (staff or an org steward, else 403) then chat_access with the owner pool; /proposal uses proposal_chat_access (thread id must be the caller's proposal chat on a readable org, else 404; readers who cannot edit get 403; claims the thread with use_case proposal and sets chat_proposal from the thread). The checks also set chat_user_id and chat_scope for tracing and tools.

ci.yml runs on every pull_request and every push to master with read-only contents permission, per-ref concurrency that cancels superseded runs, and per-job timeouts. It has four independent jobs: backend-lint (uv sync --frozen, ruff check), backend-unit (pytest -m 'not integration' with coverage), backend-integration (pgvector pg17 service, db/init SQL, app.db.migrate, seed.seed and seed.taxonomy_seed, then pytest -m integration), and frontend (Node 22, npm ci, lint, tsc --noEmit, build). It deploys nothing.

The integration job treats skips as failures to notice (pytest -rs) and deselects the two test_migration_integrity tests that need a restore of the original 96-document dump, which make seed never creates; both test jobs upload coverage.xml to Codecov with distinct flags (backend-unit, backend-integration) using OIDC except on fork PRs, which fall back to tokenless upload.

codecov.yml merges the unit and integration uploads into one report per commit (carryforward on every flag); the project status uses target auto with a 1% threshold (a PR may not lower total coverage by more than 1%) and the patch status requires 70% of added or changed lines; a fixes rule maps app/ to backend/app/ because coverage paths are relative to backend/.

backend/pyproject.toml supports CI with a pinned ruff==0.16.8 and pytest-cov in the dev group, ruff line length 110 with B008, RUF012 and UP046 ignored, and coverage configured for app with branch coverage and relative file paths.

dependency-review.yml runs actions/dependency-review-action@v4 on every pull request with fail-on-severity high and comments a summary only on failure; it fails a PR whose lockfile changes add a package with a high or critical advisory and checks only what the PR changes.

deploy.yml is the only deploy path and is triggered only by workflow_dispatch (run by hand); CI is separate and deploys nothing. The shipped CI differs from the revised plan doc: coverage goes to Codecov rather than a coverage job with diff-cover and fail_under, and only ci.yml, dependency-review.yml and deploy.yml exist under .github/workflows (no Dependabot config or Claude review workflow files are present).

Makefile: bare make runs help (built from ## comments); ENV=local|staging selects the database and deploys nothing; make evals runs golden-question evals through the real agent on the host venv at real cost, takes TAG and K selectors, and sets LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT=eval and the git sha as release; the wiki targets drive a pinned openwiki@0.7.2. Evals are not run in CI.

compare_fit(org_id) without funder_ids returns a text shortlist: the header counts only scored funders, the top FULL_DETAIL_MAX (10) strong or medium funders are shown in full, every other scored funder is on one line with score, tier and first gap, then not-scored funders; with funder_ids every named funder is rendered in full with its summary. This replaced a single JSON line of every funder that exceeded deepagents' 20k-token eviction limit and became an unpageable file.

clear_old_tool_results() uses SteppedClearToolUsesEdit with a 60,000-token trigger (was 40,000), keeping the last 5 tool results and reclaiming ceil((tokens-trigger)/20,000)*20,000 from the oldest end, so the cleared set and cached prompt prefix move once per 20k step instead of every call; compare_fit results are never cleared. The function is shared by Ask, Sangam Import and the proposal agent.

Ask efficiency status: the CHANGELOG still marks M1 (eval RunStats, max_calls budgets, ask-golden Langfuse experiment) and M2 (compare_fit text shortlist and stepped clearing) as unmerged even though their code is in the tree; M4 is merged (fetch_url removed, Ask registers six tools); M3 and M5 of the plan are not implemented (no TABLE_MAP or __cite__ columns, no Pitch prefill guard).

Ask is bounded in code by ask_model_call_limit (default 25, ASK_MODEL_CALL_LIMIT) through model_call_cap, which ends a turn that has made that many model calls, and by CompareFitBudget, which refuses a repeated compare_fit with the same arguments and any call beyond 3 per turn.
